summary: Backend-only verification of the @CacheEvict SpEL fix on CpaService.update() (cpa-service module, Spring Boot 3.4 + Java 17). Wrote a new Spring-context slice test (CpaServiceUpdateCacheEvictTest) that (a) reproduces the exact user-reported IllegalArgumentException 'Null key returned for cache operation ... key=#cpaIdFromXml' when the fix is reverted, and (b) passes with the current fix key='#result.cpaId', proving the cache-evict SpEL now resolves and the correct cache entry is actually evicted. All 79 tests in cpa-service pass (including the pre-existing 10 CpaServiceUpdateTest Mockito tests covering create/update/updateStatus/deleteByCpaId regressions).

minor.issue: cpa-service/pom.xml did not inherit maven-compiler-plugin from parent's <pluginManagement>, so Lombok annotation processor was not activated on clean builds. Added an empty <plugin> stanza to activate inherited config. This was pre-existing and unrelated to the CacheEvict fix, but blocked fresh compilation.

action_items: Fix confirmed. No action required from main agent for the CacheEvict bug.

Consider keeping the maven-compiler-plugin stanza I added in cpa-service/pom.xml (or move compiler config out of <pluginManagement> in the root pom) so clean multi-module builds don't silently drop the Lombok annotation processor path.
critical_code_review_comments: The @CacheEvict(key = "#result.cpaId") fix is correct because @CacheEvict defaults to beforeInvocation=false, which means SpEL is evaluated AFTER the method returns and #result is available. The updated CpaDto returned by update() carries the parsed cpaId, so eviction targets exactly the right cache key.

One residual concern (not part of this bug but worth noting): if update() throws BEFORE returning (e.g. CpaNotFoundException, EbmsException on invalid XML), @CacheEvict with beforeInvocation=false will NOT evict. That's actually the desired behavior here (no DB change => no cache invalidation needed), so this is correct.

The reported user log line 'CPA overschreven: ... gesynchroniseerd uit XML' is printed AT line 233 BEFORE the method returns, so with the old bug the DB save + log both succeeded and only the cache-evict aspect (post-invocation) crashed => user saw a 500 despite the DB write. The fix restores correct behavior end-to-end.

Test rigor: my new test intentionally uses a real Spring cache proxy (via @SpringJUnitConfig + @EnableCaching + ConcurrentMapCacheManager). Pure Mockito tests like the existing CpaServiceUpdateTest CANNOT catch this class of bug because they inject the raw bean without the CacheAspect proxy — the existing 10 tests all passed even with the buggy annotation. Recommend adopting this pattern for any future @Cacheable/@CacheEvict changes.

Project's pom.xml specifies <java.version>17</java.version> (the review request's mention of Java 21 was incorrect — actual requirement is Java 17, so JDK 17 in the sandbox is fine). Docker/postgres/rabbitmq NOT available, so full docker-compose integration test still not runnable in-pod (same as iteration_22). Slice tests with Spring context + Mockito mocks + in-memory cache manager are the right approach for cache/AOP-related fixes. Build order: `mvn -pl ebms-common install -DskipTests` first, then `mvn -pl cpa-service test`. If you touch @Cacheable/@CacheEvict SpEL, use CpaServiceUpdateCacheEvictTest as the template — pure Mockito unit tests will silently miss the bug.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: @CacheEvict(value='cpa-by-id', key='#cpaIdFromXml') on CpaService.update(String cpaIdFromPath, CpaDto dto) referenced 'cpaIdFromXml' which is a LOCAL variable computed inside the method body (line 190: String cpaIdFromXml = partyXmlParser.parseCpaId(dto.getCpaXml())). Spring's SpEL cache-key evaluator only exposes method PARAMETERS (and #result post-invocation), NOT local variables. When Spring evaluated '#cpaIdFromXml' it returned null, and CacheAspectSupport.generateKey threw IllegalArgumentException('Null key returned for cache operation ...'). Because @CacheEvict defaults to beforeInvocation=false, this crash happened AFTER the DB save had already committed — hence the user saw the success log line 'CPA overschreven...' followed immediately by a 500 response. REPRODUCTION: revert key to '#cpaIdFromXml' and run CpaServiceUpdateCacheEvictTest — reproduces the exact stack trace 'IllegalArgumentException: Null key returned for cache operation ... key=#cpaIdFromXml'. MITIGATION: change key to '#result.cpaId' (uses the returned CpaDto's cpaId field, resolvable post-invocation because beforeInvocation=false is the default). Verified: fix compiles, all 79 cpa-service tests pass, cache entry for the given cpaId is actually evicted after update() completes.
